What comes up in Wyong

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table describes how these jobs generally go in this area. Your block may not match it, which is the reason for looking at it first.

Farm shed and outbuilding sheeting

The semi rural blocks around Wyong carry cement sheet roofing, wall panels and fencing that has been exposed for decades.

How it is handled
Condition assessed first, removed whole where possible and never broken up on site, then wrapped, labelled and taken to a licensed facility.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists, licence class set by the condition rather than the material.

Older town house eaves and roofing

Wyong town stock is largely pre 1990, which puts bonded material in the eaves, the roof and the external sheeting until a sample says otherwise.

How it is handled
Removed sheet by sheet rather than broken, kept wet where required, and the area cleaned down before clearance.
What does it
Licensed removalists, with an independent assessor issuing clearance.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Wyong

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Older town stock Pre 1990 housing where bonded material is assumed until tested.
  • Semi rural sheds and outbuildings Fibro sheeting and roofing, frequently weathered by exposure.
  • Weathered material Which may have to be handled as friable rather than bonded.
  • Room to work on most blocks Which helps with wrapping, staging and loading.

Wyong and the surrounding blocks generally have space, so material does not have to be carried far and the set up is straightforward. Haul distance to a licensed facility is the thing worth planning here, because it is set by the classification rather than by proximity.

Wyong questions

What people ask before we start

The shed roof is cracked and crumbling. Is that still bonded asbestos?
Possibly not. Badly weathered or damaged cement sheet can have to be handled as friable, which means a different licence class, tighter controls and air monitoring. That assessment is made on site rather than assumed.
Can you dispose of material I have already removed?
Asbestos has to be wrapped, transported and disposed of at a licensed facility by someone permitted to do it. Removal that has already happened without controls is a different conversation, and it is worth having before anything is moved.
The street is narrow and the block is steep. What can get in?
Smaller plant working for longer, with spoil taken out as it is generated. On the beachside streets a truck and dog frequently is not an option, so the same volume goes out in more tipper loads.
Who signs off that the asbestos is gone?
An independent licensed assessor, not the removalist and not us. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, the removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the clearance is arranged as part of the same job.
